sanskrit: dhanūṃṣi teṣām iṣudhīn hayān dhvajān; rathāṃś ca sūtāṃś ca dhanaṃjayaḥ śaraiḥ samaṃ ca ciccheda parābhinac ca tāñ; śarottamair dvādaśabhiś ca sūtajam
english: Their bows, their quivers, their horses, their banners, their chariots and their drivers Dhanaṃjaya at once cut to pieces with his arrows and struck them down; and with twelve choice shafts he pierced the son of the charioteer.

sanskrit: athābhyadhāvaṃs tvaritāḥ śataṃ rathāḥ; śataṃ ca nāgārjunam ātatāyinaḥ śakās tukhārā yavanāś ca sādinaḥ; sahaiva kāmbojavarair jighāṃsavaḥ
english: Then a hundred chariots and a hundred elephants rushed swiftly upon Arjuna, weapons drawn to kill, and the Śakas, the Tukhāras, the Yavanas and their horsemen, together with the foremost Kāmbojas, eager to slay him.

sanskrit: varāyudhān pāṇigatān karaiḥ saha; kṣurair nyakṛntaṃs tvaritāḥ śirāṃsi ca hayāṃś ca nāgāṃś ca rathāṃś ca yudhyatāṃ; dhanaṃjayaḥ śatrugaṇaṃ tam akṣiṇot
english: Their fine weapons grasped in their hands, hands and all, and their heads he swiftly sheared off with his razor-edged shafts; and the horses, the elephants and the chariots of those who fought—Dhanaṃjaya wiped out that whole host of foes.

sanskrit: tato 'ntarikṣe suratūryanisvanāḥ; sasādhuvādā hṛṣitaiḥ samīritāḥ nipetur apy uttamapuṣpavṛṣṭayaḥ; surūpagandhāḥ pavaneritāḥ śivāḥ
english: Then in the sky the divine drums sounded, set ringing by the delighted ones with cries of 'Well done!', and showers of the choicest flowers fell, fair of form and fragrance, auspicious, borne on the wind.

sanskrit: tad adbhutaṃ devamanuṣyasākṣikaṃ; samīkṣya bhūtāni visiṣmiyur nṛpa tavātmajaḥ sūtasutaś ca na vyathāṃ; na vismayaṃ jagmatur ekaniścayau
english: Beholding that marvel, witnessed by gods and men alike, the creatures were filled with wonder, O king; yet your son and the charioteer's son felt neither dismay nor astonishment, both fixed in a single resolve.

sanskrit: athābravīd droṇasutas tavātmajaṃ; karaṃ kareṇa pratipīḍya sāntvayan prasīda duryodhana śāmya pāṇḍavair; alaṃ virodhena dhig astu vigraham
english: Then the son of Droṇa spoke to your son, pressing his hand with his own to soothe him: 'Relent, Duryodhana, make peace with the Pāṇḍavas; enough of this enmity—a curse upon this war!'

sanskrit: hato gurur brahmasamo mahāstravit; tathaiva bhīṣmapramukhā nararṣabhāḥ ahaṃ tv avadhyo mama cāpi mātulaḥ; praśādhi rājyaṃ saha pāṇḍavaiś ciram
english: 'Slain is the preceptor, the equal of Brahmā, knower of the great weapons, and likewise those bulls among men led by Bhīṣma; but I cannot be slain, nor can my uncle—so rule the kingdom long together with the Pāṇḍavas.'

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayaḥ sthāsyati vārito mayā; janārdano naiva virodham icchati yudhiṣṭhiro bhūtahite sadā rato; vṛkodaras tadvaśagas tathā yamau
english: 'Dhanaṃjaya will stand down when restrained by me; Janārdana himself desires no quarrel; Yudhiṣṭhira is ever bent on the welfare of beings, Vṛkodara obeys his will, and so too the twins.'

sanskrit: tvayā ca pārthaiś ca paraspareṇa; prajāḥ śivaṃ prāpnuyur icchati tvayi vrajantu śeṣāḥ svapurāṇi pārthivā; nivṛttavairāś ca bhavantu sainikāḥ
english: 'Should you and the sons of Pṛthā be reconciled with one another, the people would find peace, for it lies with you; let the surviving kings depart to their own cities, and let the soldiers lay aside their feuds.'

sanskrit: na ced vacaḥ śroṣyasi me narādhipa; dhruvaṃ prataptāsi hato 'ribhir yudhi idaṃ ca dṛṣṭaṃ jagatā saha tvayā; kṛtaṃ yad ekena kirīṭamālinā yathā na kuryād balabhinna cāntako; na ca pracetā bhagavān na yakṣarāṭ
english: 'But if you will not heed my words, O lord of men, surely you shall come to grief, struck down by your enemies in battle; and this you have seen, together with the whole world—what the diadem-crowned one has wrought single-handed, such as neither Indra the smasher of Bala, nor Death, nor the lord Varuṇa, nor the king of the Yakṣas could do.'

sanskrit: ato 'pi bhūyāṃś ca guṇair dhanaṃjayaḥ; sa cābhipatsyaty akhilaṃ vaco mama tavānuyātrāṃ ca tathā kariṣyati; prasīda rājañ jagataḥ śamāya vai
english: 'And Dhanaṃjaya is greater still in virtues than this, and he will accept my counsel entire and will fall in line behind you; relent, O king, for the peace of the world.'

sanskrit: mamāpi mānaḥ paramaḥ sadā tvayi; bravīmy atas tvāṃ paramāc ca sauhṛdāt nivārayiṣyāmi hi karṇam apy ahaṃ; yadā bhavān sapraṇayo bhaviṣyati
english: 'Highest is my regard for you always; therefore do I speak to you, and out of the deepest affection; for I will hold back even Karṇa, once you have become friendly.'

sanskrit: vadanti mitraṃ sahajaṃ vicakṣaṇās; tathaiva sāmnā ca dhanena cārjitam pratāpataś copanataṃ caturvidhaṃ; tad asti sarvaṃ tvayi pāṇḍaveṣu ca
english: 'The wise declare a friend to be of four kinds—the inborn, the one won by conciliation, the one won by wealth, and the one brought near by valor; and all four exist between you and the Pāṇḍavas.'

sanskrit: nisargatas te tava vīra bāndhavāḥ; punaś ca sāmnā ca samāpnuhi sthiram tvayi prasanne yadi mitratām iyur; dhruvaṃ narendrendra tathā tvam ācara
english: 'By nature they are your kinsmen, O hero; win them firmly again by conciliation. If, when you are gracious, they would come to friendship, then surely act so, O king of kings.'

sanskrit: sa evam uktaḥ suhṛdā vaco hitaṃ; vicintya niḥśvasya ca durmanābravīt yathā bhavān āha sakhe tathaiva tan; mamāpi ca jñāpayato vacaḥ śṛṇu
english: Thus addressed by his friend with these salutary words, he pondered, sighed, and, downcast, replied: 'It is just as you say, my friend; yet hear too what I, who would make my own mind known, have to say.'

sanskrit: nihatya duḥśāsanam uktavān bahu; prasahya śārdūlavad eṣa durmatiḥ vṛkodaras tad dhṛdaye mama sthitaṃ; na tatparokṣaṃ bhavataḥ kutaḥ śamaḥ
english: 'Having slain Duḥśāsana, that evil-minded Vṛkodara spoke much by force, like a tiger; that stands fixed in my heart—it is not hidden from you—so how can there be peace?'

sanskrit: na cāpi karṇaṃ guruputra saṃstavād; upāramety arhasi vaktum acyuta śrameṇa yukto mahatādya phalgunas; tam eṣa karṇaḥ prasabhaṃ haniṣyati
english: 'And out of regard, O son of the preceptor, you ought not, O steadfast one, tell Karṇa to desist; Phalguna is worn out today with great toil, and this Karṇa will slay him by main force.'

sanskrit: tam evam uktvābhyanunīya cāsakṛt; tavātmajaḥ svān anuśāsti sainikān samāghnatābhidravatāhitān imān; sabāṇaśabdān kim u joṣam āsyate
english: Having spoken thus to him, and pressed him again and again, your son commanded his own soldiers: 'Strike, charge these foes, with the twang of bowstrings—why should we stand idle?'

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tau śaṅkhabherīninade samṛddhe; samīyatuḥ śvetahayau narāgryau vaikartanaḥ sūtaputro 'rjunaś ca; durmantrite tava putrasya rājan
english: Saṃjaya said: As the blare of conch and kettledrum swelled, those two foremost of men, whose horses were white, met together—Vaikartana the charioteer's son and Arjuna—through the ill counsel of your son, O king.

sanskrit: yathā gajau haimavatau prabhinnau; pragṛhya dantāv iva vāśitārthe tathā samājagmatur ugravegau; dhanaṃjayaś cādhirathiś ca vīrau
english: As two Himālayan elephants in rut, tusks lowered, close for the sake of a she-elephant, so those two heroes of dreadful speed came together—Dhanaṃjaya and the son of the charioteer.

sanskrit: balāhakeneva yathā balāhako; yadṛcchayā vā giriṇā girir yathā tathā dhanurjyātalaneminisvanau; samīyatus tāv iṣuvarṣavarṣiṇau
english: As cloud closes with cloud, or as by chance mountain with mountain, so those two, ringing with the slap of bowstring against guard and the rim of the wheels, met, raining down showers of arrows.

sanskrit: pravṛddhaśṛṅgadrumavīrudoṣadhī; pravṛddhanānāvidhaparvataukasau yathācalau vā galitau mahābalau; tathā mahāstrair itaretaraṃ ghnataḥ
english: Like two mountains broken loose, mighty, their swelling peaks dense with trees, creepers and herbs, and teeming with all manner of mountain-dwelling beasts, so did they smite one another with their great weapons.

sanskrit: sa saṃnipātas tu tayor mahān abhūt; sureśavairocanayor yathā purā śarair vibhugnāṅganiyantṛvāhanaḥ; suduḥsaho 'nyaiḥ paṭuśoṇitodakaḥ
english: And that clash of theirs was vast, like that of the lord of the gods and the son of Virocana of old—its waters a sharp flood of blood, with limbs, drivers and mounts shattered by arrows, unbearable to any other.

sanskrit: prabhūtapadmotpalamatsyakacchapau; mahāhradau pakṣigaṇānunāditau susaṃnikṛṣṭāv aniloddhatau yathā; tathā rathau tau dhvajinau samīyatuḥ
english: As two great lakes, rich in lotuses and lilies, fish and turtles, loud with flocks of birds, drawn near and lashed up by the wind, so those two banner-bearing chariots met.

sanskrit: ubhau mahendrasya samānavikramāv; ubhau mahendrapratimau mahārathau mahendravajrapratimaiś ca sāyakair; mahendravṛtrāv iva saṃprajahratuḥ
english: Both equal in valor to great Indra, both the likeness of great Indra, mighty car-warriors, with shafts like the thunderbolt of great Indra they struck at each other, as Indra and Vṛtra of old.

sanskrit: sanāgapattyaśvarathe ubhe bale; vicitravarṇābharaṇāmbarasraje cakampatuś connamataḥ sma vismayād; viyadgatāś cārjunakarṇasaṃyuge
english: Both armies, with their elephants, foot, horse and chariots, their garlands, garments and ornaments of varied hue, trembled and reared up in wonder, as did those who watched from the sky, at the clash of Arjuna and Karṇa.

sanskrit: bhujāḥ savajrāṅgulayaḥ samucchritāḥ; sasiṃhanādā hṛṣitair didṛkṣubhiḥ yadārjunaṃ mattam iva dvipo dvipaṃ; samabhyayād ādhirathir jighāṃsayā
english: Arms with thunderbolt-fingers were raised aloft, with lions' roars, by the delighted onlookers, when the son of the charioteer bore down upon Arjuna, eager to slay him, as one rutting elephant upon another.

sanskrit: abhyakrośan somakās tatra pārthaṃ; tvarasva yāhy arjuna vidhya karṇam chindhy asya mūrdhānam alaṃ cireṇa; śraddhāṃ ca rājyād dhṛtarāṣṭrasūnoḥ
english: There the Somakas cried out to the son of Pṛthā: 'Make haste, go forth, Arjuna, pierce Karṇa! Sever his head—no more delay!—and cut off the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's hope of the kingdom!'

sanskrit: tathāsmākaṃ bahavas tatra yodhāḥ; karṇaṃ tadā yāhi yāhīty avocan jahy arjunaṃ karṇa tataḥ sacīrāḥ; punar vanaṃ yāntu cirāya pārthāḥ
english: And many warriors of ours called out then to Karṇa: 'On! On!'—'Slay Arjuna, Karṇa, and then let the sons of Pṛthā go back to the forest in their bark garments for a long age!'

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇaḥ prathamaṃ tatra pārthaṃ; maheṣubhir daśabhiḥ paryavidhyat tam arjunaḥ pratyavidhyac chitāgraiḥ; kakṣāntare daśabhir atīva kruddhaḥ
english: Then Karṇa first pierced the son of Pṛthā there with ten great arrows; and Arjuna, exceedingly wroth, pierced him back with ten sharp-pointed shafts in the side, between the armpits.

sanskrit: parasparaṃ tau viśikhaiḥ sutīkṣṇais; tatakṣatuḥ sūtaputro 'rjunaś ca parasparasyāntarepsū vimarde; subhīmam abhyāyayatuḥ prahṛṣṭau
english: With keenly sharpened shafts the two—the charioteer's son and Arjuna—gashed each other, and, seeking each an opening in the other, advanced upon one another in dreadful conflict, exulting.

sanskrit: amṛṣyamāṇaś ca mahāvimarde; tatrākrudhyad bhīmaseno mahātmā athābravīt pāṇinā pāṇim āghnan; saṃdaṣṭauṣṭho nṛtyati vādayann iva kathaṃ nu tvāṃ sūtaputraḥ kirīṭin; maheṣubhir daśabhir avidhyad agre
english: Unable to bear it in that great fray, the great-souled Bhīmasena grew enraged there, and, striking palm against palm, biting his lip, dancing as it were and clapping out a beat, he cried: 'How, O diadem-crowned one, did the charioteer's son pierce you first with ten great arrows?'

sanskrit: yayā dhṛtyā sarvabhūtāny ajaiṣīr; grāsaṃ dadad vahnaye khāṇḍave tvam tayā dhṛtyā sūtaputraṃ jahi tvam; ahaṃ vainaṃ gadayā pothayiṣye
english: 'With that resolve by which you vanquished all creatures, giving them as food to the fire at Khāṇḍava, with that resolve do you slay the charioteer's son—or else I will crush him with my mace.'

sanskrit: athābravīd vāsudevo 'pi pārthaṃ; dṛṣṭvā ratheṣūn pratihanyamānān amīmṛdat sarvathā te 'dya karṇo; hy astrair astrāṇi kim idaṃ kirīṭin
english: Then Vāsudeva too spoke to the son of Pṛthā, seeing his arrows beaten back on the car: 'Karṇa today has utterly worn down your shafts, weapon against weapon—what is this, O diadem-crowned one?'

sanskrit: sa vīra kiṃ muhyasi nāvadhīyase; nadanty ete kuravaḥ saṃprahṛṣṭāḥ karṇaṃ puraskṛtya vidur hi sarve; tvadastram astrair vinipātyamānam
english: 'O hero, why are you bewildered, why so unmindful? These Kauravas roar in their delight, putting Karṇa to the fore; for all of them have seen your weapon struck down by his weapons.'

sanskrit: yayā dhṛtyā nihataṃ tāmasāstraṃ; yuge yuge rākṣasāś cāpi ghorāḥ dambhodbhavāś cāsurāś cāhaveṣu; tayā dhṛtyā tvaṃ jahi sūtaputram
english: 'With that resolve by which the weapon of darkness was overcome, and the dread Rākṣasas age after age, and Dambhodbhava and the Asuras in their battles, with that resolve do you slay the charioteer's son.'

sanskrit: anena vāsya kṣuraneminādya; saṃchinddhi mūrdhānam areḥ prasahya mayā nisṛṣṭena sudarśanena; vajreṇa śakro namucer ivāreḥ
english: 'Or with this razor-rimmed discus Sudarśana, hurled by me, sever today by force the head of this foe, as Śakra severed that of his enemy Namuci with the thunderbolt.'

sanskrit: kirātarūpī bhagavān yayā ca; tvayā mahatyā paritoṣito 'bhūt tāṃ tvaṃ dhṛtiṃ vīra punar gṛhītvā; sahānubandhaṃ jahi sūtaputram
english: 'And that great resolve by which the Lord in the form of a Kirāta was won over by you—taking up that resolve once more, O hero, slay the charioteer's son with all his train.'

sanskrit: tato mahīṃ sāgaramekhalāṃ tvaṃ; sapattanāṃ grāmavatīṃ samṛddhām prayaccha rājñe nihatārisaṃghāṃ; yaśaś ca pārthātulam āpnuhi tvam
english: 'Then bestow upon the king this earth girdled by the sea, with her cities, rich in villages and prosperous, her hosts of foes destroyed, and win for yourself, O son of Pṛthā, glory beyond compare.'

sanskrit: saṃcodito bhīmajanārdanābhyāṃ; smṛtvā tadātmānam avekṣya sattvam mahātmanaś cāgamane viditvā; prayojanaṃ keśavam ity uvāca
english: Spurred on by Bhīma and Janārdana, recollecting himself then and surveying his own strength, and knowing the purpose behind the great-souled one's coming, Arjuna spoke thus to Keśava:

sanskrit: prāduṣkaromy eṣa mahāstram ugraṃ; śivāya lokasya vadhāya sauteḥ tan me 'nujānātu bhavān surāś ca; brahmā bhavo brahmavidaś ca sarve
english: 'I now bring forth this great and terrible weapon, for the welfare of the world and for the slaying of the charioteer's son; for this let me have leave from you, and from the gods, from Brahmā, from Bhava, and from all who know the Brahman.'

sanskrit: ity ūcivān brāhmam asahyam astraṃ; prāduścakre manasā saṃvidheyam tato diśaś ca pradiśaś ca sarvāḥ; samāvṛṇot sāyakair bhūritejāḥ sasarja bāṇān bharatarṣabho 'pi; śataṃśatān ekavad āśuvegān
english: Having spoken thus, he brought forth, governed by his mind, the unbearable Brāhma weapon; then that one of abundant splendor veiled all the quarters and intermediate quarters with his shafts, and the bull of the Bhāratas loosed his arrows by the hundredfold, as if they were one, of headlong speed.

sanskrit: vaikartanenāpi tathājimadhye; sahasraśo bāṇagaṇā visṛṣṭāḥ te ghoṣiṇaḥ pāṇḍavam abhyupeyuḥ; parjanyamuktā iva vāridhārāḥ
english: By Vaikartana likewise, there in the midst of battle, were loosed masses of arrows by the thousand; roaring, they bore down upon the Pāṇḍava, like streams of water released by the rain-cloud.

sanskrit: sa bhīmasenaṃ ca janārdanaṃ ca; kirīṭinaṃ cāpy amanuṣyakarmā tribhis tribhir bhīmabalo nihatya; nanāda ghoraṃ mahatā svareṇa
english: He of more-than-human deeds and terrible strength struck Bhīmasena, and Janārdana, and the diadem-crowned one as well, each with three shafts, and roared dreadfully in a mighty voice.

sanskrit: sa karṇabāṇābhihataḥ kirīṭī; bhīmaṃ tathā prekṣya janārdanaṃ ca amṛṣyamāṇaḥ punar eva pārthaḥ; śarān daśāṣṭau ca samudbabarha
english: Struck by Karṇa's arrows, the diadem-crowned one, gazing upon Bhīma and Janārdana so wounded, could not bear it; and the son of Pṛthā once more drew forth eighteen shafts.

sanskrit: suṣeṇam ekena śareṇa viddhvā; śalyaṃ caturbhis tribhir eva karṇam tataḥ sumuktair daśabhir jaghāna; sabhāpatiṃ kāñcanavarmanaddham
english: Piercing Suṣeṇa with one arrow, Śalya with four, and Karṇa with three, he then slew with ten well-loosed shafts the lord of the assembly, clad in golden mail.

sanskrit: sa rājaputro viśirā vibāhur; vivājisūto vidhanur viketuḥ tato rathāgrād apatat prabhagnaḥ; paraśvadhaiḥ śāla ivābhikṛttaḥ
english: That prince, headless, armless, bereft of horses and driver, of bow and standard, fell broken from the front of his chariot, like a śāla tree hewn down with axes.

sanskrit: punaś ca karṇaṃ tribhir aṣṭabhiś ca; dvābhyāṃ caturbhir daśabhiś ca viddhvā catuḥśatān dviradān sāyudhīyān; hatvā rathān aṣṭaśataṃ jaghāna sahasram aśvāṃś ca punaś ca sādīn; aṣṭau sahasrāṇi ca pattivīrān
english: And again, piercing Karṇa with three, with eight, with two, with four and with ten, and slaying four hundred war-elephants with their fighters, he struck down eight hundred chariots, a thousand horses and their riders too, and eight thousand foot-warriors.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvājimukhyāv atha yudhyamānau; didṛkṣavaḥ śūravarāv arighnau karṇaṃ ca pārthaṃ ca niyamya vāhān; khasthā mahīsthāś ca janāvatasthuḥ
english: Beholding then the two foremost of the fight, those best of heroes, slayers of foes, locked in battle, men eager to watch—those in the sky and those on earth—reined in their mounts and stood still over Karṇa and the son of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: tato dhanurjyā sahasātikṛṣṭā; sughoṣam ācchidyata pāṇḍavasya tasmin kṣaṇe sūtaputras tu pārthaṃ; samācinot kṣudrakāṇāṃ śatena
english: Then the bowstring of the Pāṇḍava, drawn back with a sudden mighty pull, snapped with a loud report; and in that instant the charioteer's son covered the son of Pṛthā with a hundred small arrows.

sanskrit: nirmuktasarpapratimaiś ca tīkṣṇais; tailapradhautaiḥ khagapatravājaiḥ ṣaṣṭyā nārācair vāsudevaṃ bibheda; tadantaraṃ somakāḥ prādravanta
english: And with sixty iron shafts, sharp as serpents newly sloughed, washed in oil and winged with the feathers of birds, he pierced Vāsudeva; and in that interval the Somakas rushed forward.

sanskrit: tato dhanurjyām avadhamya śīghraṃ; śarān astān ādhirather vidhamya susaṃrabdhaḥ karṇaśarakṣatāṅgo; raṇe pārthaḥ somakān pratyagṛhṇāt na pakṣiṇaḥ saṃpatanty antarikṣe; kṣepīyasāstreṇa kṛte 'ndhakāre
english: Then, swiftly restringing his bow and scattering the arrows the son of the charioteer had loosed, the son of Pṛthā, in great fury, his body torn by Karṇa's shafts, took up the Somakas in battle; not even the birds could fly through the sky, so was the darkness made by his swifter weapon.

sanskrit: śalyaṃ ca pārtho daśabhiḥ pṛṣatkair; bhṛśaṃ tanutre prahasann avidhyat tataḥ karṇaṃ dvādaśabhiḥ sumuktair; viddhvā punaḥ saptabhir abhyavidhyat
english: And the son of Pṛthā, laughing, pierced Śalya hard through the armor with ten shafts; then, piercing Karṇa with twelve well-loosed arrows, he struck him again with seven.

sanskrit: sa pārthabāṇāsanaveganunnair; dṛḍhāhataḥ patribhir ugravegaiḥ vibhinnagātraḥ kṣatajokṣitāṅgaḥ; karṇo babhau rudra ivātateṣuḥ
english: Struck hard by the feathered shafts of fearsome speed, driven by the force of the son of Pṛthā's bow, his body riven, his limbs bathed in blood, Karṇa shone like Rudra with his bow drawn.

sanskrit: tatas tribhiś ca tridaśādhipopamaṃ; śarair bibhedādhirathir dhanaṃjayam śarāṃs tu pañca jvalitān ivoragān; pravīrayām āsa jighāṃsur acyute
english: Then with three arrows the son of the charioteer pierced Dhanaṃjaya, the equal of the lord of the thirty gods, and, bent on slaying him, launched five shafts like blazing serpents at the steadfast one.

sanskrit: te varma bhittvā puruṣottamasya; suvarṇacitraṃ nyapatan sumuktāḥ vegena gām āviviśuḥ suvegāḥ; snātvā ca karṇābhimukhāḥ pratīyuḥ
english: Well loosed, they broke through the gold-wrought armor of that best of men and fell; with great speed they entered the earth, and, bathed there, turned back again to face Karṇa.

sanskrit: tān pañcabhallais tvaritaiḥ sumuktais; tridhā tridhaikaikam athoccakarta dhanaṃjayas te nyapatan pṛthivyāṃ; mahāhayas takṣakaputrapakṣāḥ
english: Each one of them Dhanaṃjaya cut threefold and threefold again with five swift, well-loosed broad-headed arrows, and they fell to the earth—great serpents winged like the sons of Takṣaka.

sanskrit: tataḥ prajajvāla kirīṭamālī; krodhena kakṣaṃ pradahann ivāgniḥ sa karṇam ākarṇavikṛṣṭasṛṣṭaiḥ; śaraiḥ śarīrāntakarair jvaladbhiḥ marmasv avidhyat sa cacāla duḥkhād; dhairyāt tu tasthāv atimātradhairyaḥ
english: Then the diadem-and-garland-crowned one blazed up with wrath, like a fire consuming dry brushwood; with blazing, life-ending arrows drawn and loosed to the ear, he pierced Karṇa in the vital parts—and he reeled with pain, yet, by his boundless steadiness, stood firm.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaraughaiḥ pradiśo diśaś ca; raviprabhā karṇarathaś ca rājan adṛśya āsīt kupite dhanaṃjaye; tuṣāranīhāravṛtaṃ yathā nabhaḥ
english: Then, O king, with floods of arrows the quarters and the intermediate quarters, the radiance of the sun, and Karṇa's chariot became invisible, when Dhanaṃjaya was enraged—like the sky veiled in frost and mist.

sanskrit: sa cakrarakṣān atha pādarakṣān; puraḥsarān pṛṣṭhagopāṃś ca sarvān duryodhanenānumatān arighnān; samuccitān surathān sārabhūtān
english: Those guardians of the wheels, those guardians of the feet, the vanguard and all the rearguard, the slayers of foes appointed by Duryodhana, chosen out, fine charioteers, the very flower of the host—

sanskrit: dvisāhasrān samare savyasācī; kurupravīrān ṛṣabhaḥ kurūṇām kṣaṇena sarvān sarathāśvasūtān; nināya rājan kṣayam ekavīraḥ
english: —two thousand foremost warriors of the Kurus, them in battle Savyasācin, the bull of the Kurus, in a moment brought, every one, with their chariots, horses and drivers, to destruction, O king—he, a single hero.

sanskrit: athāpalāyanta vihāya karṇaṃ; tavātmajāḥ kuravaś cāvaśiṣṭāḥ hatān avākīrya śarakṣatāṃś ca; lālapyamānāṃs tanayān pitṝṃś ca
english: Then your sons and the surviving Kurus fled, abandoning Karṇa, scattering as they went the slain and the arrow-wounded—their sons and their fathers wailing aloud.

sanskrit: sa sarvataḥ prekṣya diśo viśūnyā; bhayāvadīrṇaiḥ kurubhir vihīnaḥ na vivyathe bhārata tatra karṇaḥ; pratīpam evārjunam abhyadhāvat
english: Looking about him on every side at the emptied quarters, deserted by the Kurus rent with fear, Karṇa, O Bhārata, was not dismayed there, but charged straight on against Arjuna.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato 'payātāḥ śarapātamātram; avasthitāḥ kuravo bhinnasenāḥ vidyutprakāśaṃ dadṛśuḥ samantād; dhanaṃjayāstraṃ samudīryamāṇam
english: Saṃjaya said: Then the Kurus, their ranks broken, having drawn off the space of an arrow's flight, halted, and saw on every side, gleaming like lightning, the weapon of Dhanaṃjaya being raised up.

sanskrit: tad arjunāstraṃ grasate sma vīrān; viyat tathākāśam anantaghoṣam kruddhena pārthena tadāśu sṛṣṭaṃ; vadhāya karṇasya mahāvimarde
english: That weapon of Arjuna devoured the heroes, the firmament and the boundless-roaring sky, loosed swiftly by the wrathful son of Pṛthā in the great fray, for the slaying of Karṇa.

sanskrit: rāmād upāttena mahāmahimnā; ātharvaṇenārivināśanena tad arjunāstraṃ vyadhamad dahantaṃ; pārthaṃ ca bāṇair niśitair nijaghne
english: With the Atharvaṇa weapon of great majesty, the destroyer of foes, obtained from Rāma, Karṇa scattered that burning weapon of Arjuna and struck the son of Pṛthā with sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: tato vimardaḥ sumahān babhūva; tasyārjunasyādhiratheś ca rājan anyonyam āsādayatoḥ pṛṣatkair; viṣāṇaghātair dvipayor ivograiḥ
english: Then a most mighty struggle arose, O king, between that Arjuna and the son of the charioteer, as they fell upon each other with their shafts, like two elephants with the dreadful blows of their tusks.

sanskrit: tato ripughnaṃ samadhatta karṇaḥ; susaṃśitaṃ sarpamukhaṃ jvalantam raudraṃ śaraṃ saṃyati supradhautaṃ; pārthārtham atyarthacirāya guptam
english: Then Karṇa set to his bow a foe-slaying arrow, keenly whetted, serpent-mouthed, blazing, terrible, well-burnished for the fray—meant for the son of Pṛthā and guarded over an exceedingly long time.

sanskrit: sadārcitaṃ candanacūrṇaśāyinaṃ; suvarṇanālīśayanaṃ mahāviṣam pradīptam airāvatavaṃśasaṃbhavaṃ; śiro jihīrṣur yudhi phalgunasya
english: Ever honored, resting in powdered sandalwood, lying in a golden case, of deadly venom, ablaze, sprung from the lineage of Airāvata—with it he sought to carry off Phalguna's head in the battle.

sanskrit: tam abravīn madrarājo mahātmā; vaikartanaṃ prekṣya hi saṃhiteṣum na karṇa grīvām iṣur eṣa prāpsyate; saṃlakṣya saṃdhatsva śaraṃ śiroghnam
english: To him the great-souled king of the Madras spoke, seeing Vaikartana with arrow already fixed: 'This shaft, Karṇa, will not reach the neck; take careful aim and fit a shaft that will strike the head.'

sanskrit: athābravīt krodhasaṃraktanetraḥ; karṇaḥ śalyaṃ saṃdhiteṣuḥ prasahya na saṃdhatte dviḥ śaraṃ śalya karṇo; na mādṛśāḥ śāṭhyayuktā bhavanti
english: Then, his eyes red with wrath, Karṇa, his shaft already fitted, replied to Śalya by main force: 'Karṇa does not fit an arrow twice, Śalya; men like me are not given to guile.'

sanskrit: tathaivam uktvā visasarja taṃ śaraṃ; balāhakaṃ varṣaghanābhipūjitam hato 'si vai phalguna ity avocat; tatas tvarann ūrjitam utsasarja
english: So saying, he loosed that shaft Balāhaka, honored by the dense rain-clouds, and cried, 'Phalguna, you are slain!'—then, hastening, he sent it forth with full force.

sanskrit: saṃdhīyamānaṃ bhujagaṃ dṛṣṭvā karṇena mādhavaḥ ākramya syandanaṃ padbhyāṃ balena balināṃ varaḥ
english: Seeing the serpent being fitted to the bow by Karṇa, Mādhava, best of the strong, pressed down the chariot with his feet by his strength.

sanskrit: avagāḍhe rathe bhūmau jānubhyām agaman hayāḥ tataḥ śaraḥ so 'bhyahanat kirīṭaṃ tasya dhīmataḥ
english: As the chariot sank into the earth, the horses went down upon their knees; and then that arrow struck the diadem of that wise one.

sanskrit: athārjunasyottamagātrabhūṣaṇaṃ; dharāviyaddyosalileṣu viśrutam balāstrasargottamayatnamanyubhiḥ; śareṇa mūrdhnaḥ sa jahāra sūtajaḥ
english: Then that supreme adornment of Arjuna's head, renowned through earth, sky, heaven and the waters, the son of the charioteer carried off from his brow with that shaft, through the utmost effort, force, weaponry and wrath of his loosing.

sanskrit: divākarendujvalanagrahatviṣaṃ; suvarṇamuktāmaṇijālabhūṣitam puraṃdarārthaṃ tapasā prayatnataḥ; svayaṃ kṛtaṃ yad bhuvanasya sūnunā
english: Its splendor like that of the sun, the moon, fire and the planets, adorned with a net of gold, pearls and gems—it had been fashioned with effort and austerity, for Indra's sake, by the Maker of the world himself.

sanskrit: mahārharūpaṃ dviṣatāṃ bhayaṃkaraṃ; vibhāti cātyarthasukhaṃ sugandhi tat nijaghnuṣe devaripūn sureśvaraḥ; svayaṃ dadau yat sumanāḥ kirīṭine
english: Of most precious form, terrifying to foes, exceedingly pleasant and fragrant, it shone—that which the lord of the gods, well pleased, gave with his own hand to the diadem-crowned one when he had slain the foes of the gods.

sanskrit: harāmbupākhaṇḍalavittagoptṛbhiḥ; pinākapāśāśanisāyakottamaiḥ surottamair apy aviṣahyam ardituṃ; prasahya nāgena jahāra yad vṛṣaḥ
english: That which not even Hara, Varuṇa, Indra and the lord of wealth, those best of gods, with the Pināka, the noose, the thunderbolt and their choicest shafts, could batter to harm—Karṇa carried it off by force with his serpent-arrow.

sanskrit: tad uttameṣūn mathitaṃ viṣāgninā; pradīptam arciṣmad abhikṣiti priyam papāta pārthasya kirīṭam uttamaṃ; divākaro 'stād iva parvatāj jvalan
english: Crushed by that best of shafts, kindled by the venom's fire, ablaze and flaming toward the earth, the beloved supreme diadem of the son of Pṛthā fell, like the blazing sun from the mountain of setting.

sanskrit: tataḥ kirīṭaṃ bahuratnamaṇḍitaṃ; jahāra nāgo 'rjunamūrdhato balāt gireḥ sujātāṅkurapuṣpitadrumaṃ; mahendravajraḥ śikharaṃ yathottamam
english: Then the serpent bore the diadem, adorned with many jewels, by force from Arjuna's head, as the thunderbolt of great Indra strikes the topmost peak of a mountain, with its trees in fair bud and flower.
